roads.name: Westside Road
words: Sweeping and steady: 14 curves in 3.9 miles.
From 2,817 to 2,999 ft, with 624 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every sweeper in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 80 km/h limit its corners still ask for about 0.52 g, so the curves, not the limit, set the pace.

roads.name: Kananaskis Lakes Trail
words: Properly twisty: 30 curves in 5.2 miles, about 6 a mile.
The curves flow straight into one another.
From 5,503 to 5,680 ft, with 966 ft of up and down along the way.
roads.ratingNote: A full bar is top marks for that part; the percentages are each part's share of the rating. Curves, length and up and down are ranked against every road in the library. The rest are scored on the road itself: how few side roads join it, whether the curves or the limit set the pace, and how little is built up along it. At the 50 km/h limit its curves ask for about 0.23 g.

roads.name: Banff-Windermere Parkway
words: Sweeping and steady: 45 curves in 11.4 miles.
The curves flow straight into one another.
From 2,878 to 4,865 ft, with 3,191 ft of up and down along the way.
34 parks, trailheads and other stops along it, so it's likely busier than most, especially on weekends.
